properties.Name: Sakura
properties.Description: Cute little town I stopped in on the way back from Naritansan.  They had a bamboo path and some historical samurai residences.

properties.Name: Takaosan
properties.Description: Takaosan is one of the closest mountains (599m) to Tokyo, and is still technically within the city boundaries.  It's just over an hour by direct train from my flat,  and with 6 different routes to explore I ended up coming multiple times.

properties.Name: Mitakesan
properties.Description: Roughly 2 hours from Tokyo.  A group of us came for a day trip during Golden Week, as Takaosan would have been far too crowded.

properties.Name: Naritasan
properties.Description: Naritasan Shinsho-ji is a sprawling temple complex just by the airport.  Despite being so close it never seems to end up on the popular travel itineraries,  but well worth a daytrip I think.  Purely by coindience I ended up going on the first of March when a bunch of spring festivities were being held.

properties.Name: Yokosuka
properties.Description: Yokosuka is mainly known for the US naval base. When I arrived, there were at least 30 ship-nerds on the bay taking pictures of the fleet.

properties.Name: Kurihama
properties.Description: I had no particular reason to come to Kurihama,  apart from that it was where my ferry from Chiba ended up (and I wanted to do a loop of Tokyo bay).  Apparently it's where Admiral Perry landed with his black ships.

properties.Name: Nokogiri
properties.Description: Went for a day hike up and around Nokogiri in Chiba. It was about 33 degrees and I sweated my entire bodyweight.

properties.Name: Shinjuku
properties.Description: Great for shopping - otherwise to be avoided at all costs! Getting out the station alone takes about 10 minutes.

properties.Name: Shimo-Kitazawa
properties.Description: Tokyo's "Camden", which is to say,  cool area that has been somewhat tourist and gentrfied.  It's still very nice though. Shimokitazawa is famous for its vintage clothing shops, which I personally find all prohibitively expensive,  but if you go there without intending to buy cloths it's great.

properties.Name: Koenji
properties.Description: A grungier version of Shimokitazawa. This is the place to go for more reasonably priced vintage clothing.

properties.Name: Sakura-shinmachi
properties.Description: I stayed here for 2 weeks in a tiny hostel when I initially arrived in Japan.

properties.Name: Monzen-Nagacho
properties.Description: Old-fashioned downtown neighbourhood in East Tokyo. The local temple holds a musical fire ceremony every day - well worth checking out!

properties.Name: Kagurazaka
properties.Description: Tokyo's bougie french-quarter. I stayed here for 6 weeks in Feburary.  A great central spot to explore Tokyo - a little too upmarket for my tastes though,  I felt intimidated walking into many of the shops.

properties.Name: Shibuya
properties.Description: While I was initially snobby about Shibya (too many tourists/vloggers!) it ended up becoming my main place to go out - once you get out the main station area there are some more grown up spots.

properties.Name: Mito
properties.Description: Stopped here very briefly to catch the ferry to Hokkaido.

properties.Name: Asahikawa
properties.Description: Asahikawa is Hokkaido's second largest city,  Japan's northern most major city,  and where the Japanese side of my family grew up.  I used to spend a lot of summers and winter holidays here as a kid,  at my grandma's house,  so I came to Asahikawa mostly for nostalgic reasons

properties.Name: Otaru
properties.Description: A former port town,  now turned popular tourist site.  I spent an afternoon here before boarding the ferry to Niigata.

properties.Name: Noboribetsu
properties.Description: Small onsen town near Sapporo where we stopped for 2 nights.

properties.Name: Sapporo
properties.Description: Hokkaido's largest city with 2.1 million people. I stayed with my uncle here a few times,  but forgot to record any of the walking routes I did!

properties.Name: Niigata
properties.Description: I stayed a night in Niigata,  mainly because it was the destination of my ferry.  It's a working port town and there isn't much in the way of tourist sites - the locals were quite confused as to what I was doing there.

properties.Name: Kurobe George
properties.Description: We spent a whole day travelling the tiny tourist train through the george, it was incredibly pretty.

properties.Name: Toyama
properties.Description: Came here with some friends for a few nights, on the recommendation of the New York Times "52 Places to Go in 2025" list. We were worried it would be full of tourists - as it turned out there were barely any tourists but a lot of signs proudly proclaiming the New York Times had put them in their travel list!

properties.Name: Takaoka
properties.Description: Stopped her briefly to see the big Buddah.

properties.Name: Kanazawa
properties.Description: The capital of Ishikawa Prefecture, often referred to as "Little Kyoto" for its well-preserved historical districts. It was very wet when we visited!

properties.Name: Eiheiji Temple
properties.Description: We were never meant to come here - the original plan was to visit a set of historical hamlets near Kanazawa,  but we discovered the night before that I should have booked the coach about a month in advance.  Some frantic last minute planning led us to jump on a quick shinkanzen to this monastry in Fukui. It was pouring with rain when we visited, which added to the atmospere.
